result.rationale: addGuests.schema.ts defines guests: z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness check, and the handler's uniqueGuests filter only compares guests to booking.attendees ('!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)'), never deduplicating within the input array. Duplicate emails in a direct tRPC mutation would pass validation and create duplicate attendee rows via createMany. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: The server-side uniqueness filter compares each guest against existing booking attendees but never deduplicates guests within the input array, while the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts z.array(z.string().email())) has no uniqueness refine unlike the client copy. A direct tRPC mutation with guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] passes the schema and creates two identical attendee rows for the same email, duplicating that guest on the booking and in every subsequent email/calendar sync; the client-only refine is not a security boundary.
